answer: A hardware attestation protocol curbs Sybil attacks by anchoring agents to dedicated secure silicon. Each participant routes enclave proofs across an attestation bridge, referencing a verifiable device atlas while signing telemetry via a physical walnut security token. An adversary must procure scarce, non-duplicable cryptographic coprocessors per simulated identity. However, microarchitectural side-channel exploits can allow adversaries to extract signing keys and spoof multiple nodes.
